    // The normalized sum of the octaves.
    Eval(self: FbmNoise2D, p: Point2D): Number

    Eval(self: FbmNoise3D, p: Point3D): Number
        => self.Octaves

            .Reduce(0.0, (acc, v) => acc + v)

    //==
    // # Turbulence
    //
    // The same sum over the ABSOLUTE value of each octave. Non-negative, and the
    // creases where an octave crosses zero are the billowy character the type's
    // doc comment describes.

    // The non-negative contribution of octave k.
    TurbulenceOctave(basis: NoiseBasis, seed: Integer, frequency: Number, lacunarity: Number, gain: Number, p: Point2D, k: Integer): Number
        => BasisValue2D(basis, seed + k, frequency * lacunarity.Pow(k.ToNumber), p).Abs
           * OctaveWeight(gain, k);

    // The non-negative contribution of octave k.
    TurbulenceOctave(basis: NoiseBasis, seed: Integer, frequency: Number, lacunarity: Number, gain: Number, p: Point3D, k: Integer): Number
        => BasisValue3D(basis, seed + k, frequency * lacunarity.Pow(k.ToNumber), p).Abs
           * OctaveWeight(gain, k);

    // The normalized sum of the rectified octaves; in [0, 1].
    Eval(self: TurbulenceNoise2D, p: Point2D): Number
        => self.Octaves
            .MapRange(k => TurbulenceOctave(self.Basis, self.Seed, self.Frequency, self.Lacunarity, self.Gain, p, k))
            .Reduce(0.0, (acc, v) => acc + v)
           / TotalWeight(self.Gain, self.Octaves);

    // The normalized sum of the rectified octaves; in [0, 1].
    Eval(self: TurbulenceNoise3D, p: Point3D): Number
        => self.Octaves
            .MapRange(k => TurbulenceOctave(self.Basis, self.Seed, self.Frequency, self.Lacunarity, self.Gain, p, k))
            .Reduce(0.0, (acc, v) => acc + v)
           / TotalWeight(self.Gain, self.Octaves);

    //==
    // # Ridged multifractal
    //
    // Each octave is inverted and squared: `(Offset - |basis|)^2`. The inversion
    // turns the basis's zero crossings into the maxima — the ridge lines — and
    // the square sharpens them. Non-negative; normalized by Offset^2 times the
    // weight total, which is the value a perfectly ridged sample would reach.
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multifractal_system

    // The ridged contribution of octave k.
    RidgedOctave(basis: NoiseBasis, seed: Integer, frequency: Number, lacunarity: Number, gain: Number, offset: Number, p: Point2D, k: Integer): Number {
        var signal = offset - BasisValue2D(basis, seed + k, frequency * lacunarity.Pow(k.ToNumber), p).Abs;
        return signal * signal * OctaveWeight(gain, k);
    }

    // The ridged contribution of octave k.
    RidgedOctave(basis: NoiseBasis, seed: Integer, frequency: Number, lacunarity: Number, gain: Number, offset: Number, p: Point3D, k: Integer): Number {
        var signal = offset - BasisValue3D(basis, seed + k, frequency * lacunarity.Pow(k.ToNumber), p).Abs;
        return signal * signal * OctaveWeight(gain, k);
    }

    // The scale that brings the ridged sum back to a nominal [0, 1]: the value the
    // sum reaches when every octave rides its ridge. One when Offset is zero.
    RidgedTotal(gain: Number, offset: Number, octaves: Integer): Number
        => offset == 0.0 ? 1.0 : offset * offset * TotalWeight(gain, octaves);

    // The normalized sum of the ridged octaves; nominally in [0, 1].
    Eval(self: RidgedNoise2D, p: Point2D): Number
        => self.Octaves
            .MapRange(k => RidgedOctave(self.Basis, self.Seed, self.Frequency, self.Lacunarity, self.Gain, self.Offset, p, k))
            .Reduce(0.0, (acc, v) => acc + v)
           / RidgedTotal(self.Gain, self.Offset, self.Octaves);

    // The normalized sum of the ridged octaves; nominally in [0, 1].
    Eval(self: RidgedNoise3D, p: Point3D): Number
        => self.Octaves
            .MapRange(k => RidgedOctave(self.Basis, self.Seed, self.Frequency, self.Lacunarity, self.Gain, self.Offset, p, k))
            .Reduce(0.0, (acc, v) => acc + v)
           / RidgedTotal(self.Gain, self.Offset, self.Octaves);

    //==
    // # Warped and derived noise evaluation
    //
    // The `Eval` bodies for `noise.types.plato`: domain warping, which moves
    // the sample point before evaluating the basis, and curl noise, which reads a
    // divergence-free vector field off the derivatives of a scalar (2D) or vector
    // (3D) potential.
    //
    // Iterations is a runtime count and each warp step consumes the PREVIOUS
    // displaced point, so the warp is written as a recursion rather than as the
    // MapRange + Reduce the fractal sums use — the steps do not commute and there is
    // nothing to sum.
    //
    // The curl bodies differentiate by central difference. The step is a fixed
    // 1e-3 in the field's own input units: small enough that the second-order error
    // is invisible next to the noise itself, large enough to stay well clear of
    // catastrophic cancellation in single precision.

    //==
    // # Domain warping
    //
    // Each iteration displaces the point by a warp noise sampled at the point
    // itself, so the field folds through itself repeatedly — the marbling. The
    // two (three) displacement components come from decorrelated seeds; sharing
    // one would displace every point along the diagonal.

    // The point after `remaining` further warp iterations.
    WarpPoint(basis: NoiseBasis, seed: Integer, strength: Number, frequency: Number, p: Point2D, remaining: Integer): Point2D
        => remaining <= 0
            ? p
            : WarpPoint(basis, seed, strength, frequency,
                Point2D(p.X + strength * BasisValue2D(basis, seed + 101, frequency, p),
                        p.Y + strength * BasisValue2D(basis, seed + 227, frequency, p)),
                remaining - 1);

    // The point after `remaining` further warp iterations.
    WarpPoint(basis: NoiseBasis, seed: Integer, strength: Number, frequency: Number, p: Point3D, remaining: Integer): Point3D
        => remaining <= 0
            ? p
            : WarpPoint(basis, seed, strength, frequency,
                Point3D(p.X + strength * BasisValue3D(basis, seed + 101, frequency, p),
                        p.Y + strength * BasisValue3D(basis, seed + 227, frequency, p),
                        p.Z + strength * BasisValue3D(basis, seed + 373, frequency, p)),
                remaining - 1);

    // The basis noise sampled at the warped point.
    Eval(self: DomainWarpNoise2D, p: Point2D): Number
        => BasisValue2D(self.Basis, self.Seed, self.Frequency,
            WarpPoint(self.Basis, self.Seed, self.WarpStrength, self.WarpFrequency, p, self.Iterations));

    // The basis noise sampled at the warped point.
    Eval(self: DomainWarpNoise3D, p: Point3D): Number
        => BasisValue3D(self.Basis, self.Seed, self.Frequency,
            WarpPoint(self.Basis, self.Seed, self.WarpStrength, self.WarpFrequency, p, self.Iterations));

    //==
    // # Curl noise
    //
    // The curl of a smooth potential is divergence-free by construction (the
    // divergence of a curl is identically zero), which is exactly what advecting
    // particles wants: no sources and no sinks, so density is preserved.
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Curl_(mathematics)
    //
    // Perlin noise is the potential in both dimensions: it is smooth enough that
    // the difference quotient is meaningful, unlike value or Worley noise.

    // The finite-difference step, in the field's input units.
    CurlStep(self: CurlNoise2D): Number => 0.001;

    // The finite-difference step, in the field's input units.
    CurlStep(self: CurlNoise3D): Number => 0.001;
